statement: You receive a sorted row of distinct integers and a target integer. Print the index at which the target sits if it is present; otherwise print the index at which it would be inserted to keep the row sorted. Indices start at 0. Solve it with one binary search, without scanning the row.
constraints: Values are distinct and sorted ascending.

example.why: 5 is present at index 2; a target of 4 would print 2 as well, landing before the 5.

hint: This is lower bound: the first index whose value is at least the target answers both cases at once.
mistake: Handling present and absent targets as two separate searches - one lower bound already covers both.
